newsitem.title: USA: Stocks brace for start of earnings season.
newsitem.headline: Stocks brace for start of earnings season.

text.p: Stock prices were mixed Wednesday as Wall Street braced for the flood of corporate earnings that starts next week.

At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 0.38 points at 6,608.78. In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 12-9 on active New York Stock Exchange volume of 252 million shares.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 3.54 points at 1,260.91.
Weakness in blue-chip stocks Merck & Co. and International Business Machines Corp. weighed on the Dow index.
Balancing out the weakness in the Dow was Procter & Gamble Co., up 2-7/8 at 118-3/4 after announcing its acquisition of Tambrands Inc. for $1.85 billion.
"I think we are noodling here. We are working our way through the earnings reports, which are, on balance, stronger than expected," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp.
He said that through Tuesday, of the 37 Standard & Poor's 500 companies that have reported earnings, 16 had results that exceeded Wall Street's expectations, nine were below and 12 on target.
Merck was down 3-1/4 at 82 after being downgraded by Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch and Alex. Brown. IBM was down 1 at 135-5/8.
There was more merger activity to whet investors' appetites after Procter & Gamble said it would acquire Tambrands for $50 a share, or $1.85 billion. Tambrands was up 2 at 48-1/8.

"I think it's really more of the same," Johnson said. "The deal reflects the continued efforts by companies to enhance shareholder value. We have gone through a period of restructuring, downsizing and closing obsolete plants. We have been through a period of stock repurchasing."
Johnson said Tambrands was a good fit for P&G.

"Procter & Gamble is definitely buying a company which fits its strategic needs," he said. "You've seen something similar with banks buying brokerages. Everyone is trying to boost earnings and revenues in a fairly relaxed regulatory environment."

Among special situations, Biogen Inc. fell 3 to 36-1/4 in active trade after saying the European Patent Office had revoked the company's patent covering the production of recombinant beta interferon as result of an appeal filed by Germany's Schering AG.
HBO & Co. jumped in heavy trading after the health care information company posted stronger-than-expected first quarter earnings. Shares rose 4-1/8 to 53-3/4.
Seagate Technology Inc. was up 3/8 at 51-7/8 in very active trading after posting better than forecast third quarter earnings.
